newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metway sees similar first half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metway sees similar first half profit.

text.p: Metway Bank Ltd, soon to be part of the Queensland government's plan to create a state "mega bank", said on Wednesday profit for the current half year would be similar to the first half of the last financial year.

"If Metway was to continue as a single operating entity, current indications are that profit for the half year before tax and after abnormals would be similar to the first half of last financial year," Chairman Frank Haly told the annual meeting.
Haly said net profits for the first quarter of the current year to June 30 had met budget expectations.
Group lending for the three months to the end of September this year totalled A$655.83 million, a 5.77 percent increase on the same quarter last year.
Total business banking for the period amounted to A$365.44 million an increase of A$46.46 million or 14.57 percent for the same three months in 1995/96, Haly said.
However, residential lending which totalled A$247.98 million was down 6.43 percent for the quarter, reflecting very competitive conditions in a sluggish housing industry, Haly said.
"Our strengthening position in business markets is again emphasised by sound loans volume for the three months," Haly said.
He said the banks drive into consumer lending continued to show good results with lending of A$42.41 million for the three months, up 17.5 percent on the same period last year.
Haly said if the current climate of official indictors can be repeated in coming months prospects for improved business confidence later this financial year were good.
"Directors are pleased we are delivering a well run progressive and profitable bank into the preposed merger with the Suncorp group and QIDC (Queensland Industry Development Corporation)," Haly said.
Metway shareholders are meeting this morning to vote on the preposed merger.
